labels.notes: Unmarked and partial. That is correct. The module docstring writes `thm:lower-bound` — `Yamabegap.tex:512` without the ``**`label`**`` mark. The two decl docstrings in bold (l.268, l.310) do not match tools/ledger.py's mark regex, and they follow the strict library's own style (Main.lean:784). I read the anchors against Yamabegap.tex l.512–536, hypothesis by hypothesis. (1) « Under the hypotheses of thm:upper-bound »: the anchors take them exactly as the strict, graduated upper_bound_of_gluings_of_pos reads them. That is R_g x = c for every x, MinimalBoundary, and the lem:gluing family g̃_τ with a GluingInput per τ (σ(Σ̄) ≤ 0 as y ≤ 0, OQ-93 (e)). lem:positivity is not carried: it is derived, because the anchor feeds F_g(1)/Λ_max > 0 (Fq_one_pos, Λ_max ≥ 1) into hpos. (2) thm:main's hypotheses are carried on the model and disclosed: MeanPoincare, TraceBound, InteriorBump, StarIneq A, and AbsLatticeApprox in thm_lower_bound only. Ã is universally quantified under eq:star, which is broader than « Ã depends only on … ». The _three and _starN forms discharge eq:star from valid λ and C_SP. The Mfd.Reads forms also discharge MeanPoincare, the trace bound, λ₁ > 0, C_SP < ∞ and eq:star, and carry NonConst and InteriorBump; this matches SCOPE (2). (3) θ = a_N cap*/(c_N Σ|B_j|^{(N−2)/(N−1)}) is the companion's cap* with weights w_j = |B_j|^{(N−2)/(N−1)}/S (Capacity.lean capWeight and bdryS). This is disclosed as a reading and a question. (4) κ is eq:kappa with O(F²) replaced by the explicit mainRem N θ Ã F (OQ-111 (b)). The anchor also states mainRem =O[𝓝 0] F² and the uniform 5/7 bound, and kappa_mul_Fq gives κF = F/Λ_max exactly. This is the disclosed explicit form. (5) δ = gapBdry σb g = σb − EH(Σ, g) for any real σb with hσb : 0 ≤ σb. Since σb is universally quantified, instantiating σb := σ^∂(Σ) gives the printed bound under the one added hypothesis σ^∂(Σ) ≥ 0. Instantiating σb = 0 gives the σ-free core κF ≤ −EH, and gap_ge_of_le_infF proves δ ≥ σb + b for every σb. So the hypothesis is added, disclosed, and not vacuity-making. (6) The M-form of l.522–524 is a conjunct conditional on round areas, with M := roundMass (OQ-44, DEC-186): disclosed. eq:R-bound appears before the limit as κF ≤ |c|Vol^{2/N} and κ·2(N−1)M/Vol ≤ |c|. The optimality clause, θ = 2 and θ = 1 with κ → 1/2, and the o(1) are not formalized and are disclosed (T-perf-dilute-limit). Non-vacuity: toy_thm_lower_bound exercises thm_lower_bound_signed. Probes (in /tmp, deleted) also applied the principal anchor thm_lower_bound and thm_lower_bound_three to the same toy data, with AbsLattice.approx, hstar.starIneq, λ = 4, C = 1 and σb = 0. Both typecheck, so the principal anchor's hypotheses are jointly satisfiable. The Mfd.Reads forms are not witnessed with a GluingInput family on a manifold reading. The REPORT does not claim they are, and their extra hypotheses (Reads, IsLocallyLebesgue, NonConst) are witnessed separately in the strict Poincare.lean. Bookkeeping: the label's decls (13) include helpers and the toy witness. REPORT.notes names the six anchors as the ledger decls; curate those.

docstring_contract: kb 0006 is met. Title. The label is unmarked with `Yamabegap.tex:512`, which is the \begin{theorem} line, within 4000 characters. The > quote of l.514–535 agrees with the tex up to equation delimiters (script, whitespace-normalised). The other quotes (l.538–543, eq:gap-bdry, perforated l.924–927) are as printed. Then ## Hypothesis checklist, ## SCOPE (disclosed), and the provenance line. The checklist vocabulary (✓ carried / ⚠ read / ⚠ carried / ✗ not formalized) is the strict library's. I checked every cited line and every one is right: Yamabegap 352–353, 366–369, 379–385, 467–469, 494–495, 512–536, 538–545, 547, 724–728; perforated 145, 156–170, 180, 211, 399–401, 458–460, 479, 505, 512, 602, 606–618, 680, 916–934. findings_checked: Finding 1 (σ^∂(Σ) ≥ 0 missing) is true. Yamabegap l.514 assumes only thm:upper-bound's hypotheses, and δ = σ^∂ − EH (l.352–353). The companion's argument (perforated l.924–925) concludes δ ≥ λ_∂ only « whenever Yb(Σ) ≥ 0 ». As formalized, thm:upper-bound's hypotheses cannot give it, because σ^∂ is not definable on the model. Mathematically it is also not implied by σ(Σ̄) ≤ 0. A doubling argument (argued here, not formalized) shows this. For N = 3, take any class on Σ with its csc, H = 0 representative (fact (ii)) and double across the minimal boundary. Since the mean curvatures match, the double carries metrics whose Yamabe constants tend to 2^{2/3}·Y_[g](Σ). So Y_[g](Σ) ≤ 2^{−2/3}σ(DΣ) < 0 whenever σ(DΣ) < 0, for example Σ̄ closed hyperbolic. Then σ^∂(Σ) < 0 under thm:upper-bound's hypotheses. The finding does not overreach: it reports a missing hypothesis and claims no counterexample. Its remark that eq:sigma-torus's lower half is only argued is also fair. In fact « metrics whose energy tends to zero » bounds Y_[g] from above, while σ^∂ ≥ 0 needs a lower bound on the infimum.

Finding 2 (l.522–524 holds only for round B_j) is true. M is defined only via def:reference (N = 3, positive Gauss curvature, l.379–385). With H_g = 0, M_j = ∫ H_mean(∂C_j). Minkowski's inequality ∫H_mean dA ≥ √(4πA), with equality only for the round sphere, gives c_3|B_j|^{1/2} = 4√(4π|B_j|) ≤ 4M_j. So F_g(1) ≤ 4M/Vol^{1/3}, strictly for a non-round B_j, which only needs to be conformally round under thm:upper-bound.

Finding 3 (Ã depends on V) is true. The printed eq:Atil (perforated l.606–618) contains V^{−2/3}, …, V^{−1/6} in G, and star3AtilCorr V λ C and starNAtil q c V λ C take V. Scale invariance of Ã against λ₁ ∝ s^{−2} forces dependence through λ₁V^{2/N}.

Finding 4 (optimality transfers to δ only with an upper bound) is true. thm:sharp (perforated l.211) is about λ_∂, the route to δ is the one-sided δ ≥ λ_∂, and eq:sandwich (Yamabegap l.547) gives only δ ≤ F_g(1).
Remark 5 (eq:R-bound needs no σ^∂) is true and is proved: hkR in lower_bound_of_eq_main does not use hσb.

The weights question rests on true facts. An « area-weighted » mean has weights |B_j|/Σ|B_k|. The companion's ℓ has |B_j|^{(N−2)/(N−1)}/S. They coincide iff n = 1 or all areas are equal, since 1 − 2/p♯ = 1/(N−1) ≠ 0. lem:holder's minimiser is unique (perforated l.479–494), so with area weights Σ a_j²|B_j|^{−2/p♯} > 1/S and c_N/C_2² < F_g(1): the eq:calib identity at l.512 fails. It is correctly posed as a question, not as an error.
